clause.quote: The Text, ‘T’, domain representations in CESR MUST use only the characters from the URL/filename safe variant of the IETF RFC-4648 Base64 standard[[RFC4648](#RFC4648)].

inferred_from.inference: A parser should reject a text-domain primitive that contains a character outside the URL- and filename-safe Base64 alphabet, such as the standard alphabet's '+' and '/' or the '=' pad character.
inferred_from.quote: The Text, ‘T’, domain representations in CESR MUST use only the characters from the URL/filename safe variant of the IETF RFC-4648 Base64 standard[[RFC4648](#RFC4648)].

description: After a KERI 2.0 inception, an attachments group holds a nontransferable receipt couple whose B prefix is BAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=: its last character is the Base64 pad character '=', which CESR never uses because every CESR primitive is composable. The text domain uses only the URL- and filename-safe Base64 alphabet (line 93), which has no '='. The specification states no parser-side rule for this stream; the stream breaks the cited MUST, and the assertion that a parser rejects it is graded SHOULD on the inference recorded in inferred_from.
title: Reject a text-domain primitive containing '='
